note: IPL pilot. Revenue and net profit are now MCA-filed for all ten franchises (ipl_fin_fy24 / csk_fy24) — only SRH's profit is estimated. Revenue-mix splits (central pool / own commercial / gate), brand values, market enterprise values and forward scenarios remain modeled. The central media distribution is ~₹467cr/club (₹4,670cr total, ipl_fin_fy24). Every estimated figure carries estimated:true.

economics.central_media_pool: IPL 2023-27 media rights ₹48,390cr (ipl_media_2327); franchises received ~₹4,670cr in aggregate central distribution for 2023 (~₹467cr each, ipl_fin_fy24) — this dominates revenue and makes the league structurally profitable.
economics.salary_cap: Player salary cap ~₹100cr/season — wages/revenue is uniformly low (~13-17%); cost discipline is strong league-wide.
economics.asset_light: Franchises lease stadiums from state associations — no owned stadium asset; the franchise brand is the core intangible.
economics.profitability: Nine of ten franchises were profitable in FY24. Punjab Kings was the most profitable (₹252cr, ~38% margin) despite never winning — a clean 'profit over trophies' case. Gujarat Titans was the only loss-maker (−₹57cr) despite the highest revenue (₹776cr), on an entry-fee-inflated cost base.
economics.multi_league_networks: Several owners run cross-league portfolios (Knight Riders, Mumbai Indians, Super Kings, Royals, GMR Capitals) — the Arctos cross-league thesis; captured as a growth signal and in data/portfolio-operators.json.
